items.title: [LLK] Dest->Src bank waits still miss the math-pipeline drain at 33 sites (WH + BH)
items.body:
## Summary

[PR #52256](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/52256) fixed the generic Blackhole destination-reuse handshake by adding a math-pipeline drain to the wait that gates `MOVD2A` / `MOVD2B`:

```cpp
// before
TTI_STALLWAIT(p_stall::STALL_MATH, p_stall::SRCA_VLD);
// after
TTI_STALLWAIT(p_stall::STALL_MATH, p_stall::MATH | p_stall::SRCA_VLD);
```

That fix was applied to exactly two functions in one file. The same bare wait is still present at **33 other sites across 16 files**, on both Wormhole and Blackhole, including the canonical `transpose_dest` LLK and several TTNN-private LLK copies compiled by production kernels.

This issue tracks the remaining sites. It deliberately excludes every site already covered by an open or merged PR (see *Out of scope* below), so it does not overlap [#53655](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/53655) / [PR #53690](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/53690) or [PR #54731](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/54731).

## Mechanism

`p_stall::SRCA_VLD` / `SRCB_VLD` are [`STALLWAIT`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-isa-documentation/blob/main/WormholeB0/TensixTile/TensixCoprocessor/STALLWAIT.md) conditions **C10** / **C11**:

> **C10** — keep waiting if `SrcA[MatrixUnit.SrcABank].AllowedClient != SrcClient::MatrixUnit`
> **C11** — keep waiting if `SrcB[MatrixUnit.SrcBBank].AllowedClient != SrcClient::MatrixUnit`

Both index `MatrixUnit.SrcABank` / `SrcBBank` live, at the Wait Gate. Those bank pointers are advanced in the *epilogue* of the preceding Matrix Unit instruction — the `if (FlipSrcA)` / `if (FlipSrcB)` block at the very end of [`ELWMUL`'s functional model](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-isa-documentation/blob/main/WormholeB0/TensixTile/TensixCoprocessor/ELWMUL.md#functional-model), and equivalently for `SETRWC` with a `CLR_*` operand.

So with a bank-flipping Matrix Unit instruction still in flight, C10/C11 test the *pre-flip* bank — which the Matrix Unit still owns — are satisfied vacuously, and the wait is forgotten. By the time the following `MOVD2A` / `MOVD2B` executes, the flip has landed, and it writes the *post-flip* bank: one the unpacker still owns and may be filling.

`MOVD2A` and `MOVD2B` do not auto-wait for this. Both ISA pages say so explicitly and direct software to use `STALLWAIT` with exactly these condition codes ([`MOVD2A`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-isa-documentation/blob/main/WormholeB0/TensixTile/TensixCoprocessor/MOVD2A.md#instruction-scheduling), [`MOVD2B`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-isa-documentation/blob/main/WormholeB0/TensixTile/TensixCoprocessor/MOVD2B.md#instruction-scheduling)). The ISA's own note on C10/C11 — *"rarely needed, as Matrix Unit (FPU) instructions which read from SrcA or SrcB automatically wait for this condition"* — is precisely why these Dest→Src **writes** are the exception that needs the explicit wait, and why the symptom is a silent value mismatch rather than a hang.

Adding `p_stall::MATH` selects condition **C7**:

> **C7** — keep waiting if the current thread has an instruction in any stage of the Matrix Unit (FPU) pipeline

which drains the pipe so C10/C11 observe the post-flip pointer. C7's documented requirement is that the block mask include **B6** (block new Matrix Unit instructions); every site here already passes `p_stall::STALL_MATH`, which *is* B6, so that precondition is already satisfied.

`STALLWAIT` stays latched while *any* selected condition says keep-waiting and is forgotten only once *all* are simultaneously met, so a single combined mask is correct and no extra instruction is needed. That matters for the sites recorded into the replay buffer (`generalized_moe_gate_eltwise_binary`, the `deepseek_moe_gate` variants), where the recorded instruction count must not change — it does not.

**Cost.** C7 is a real drain, and the ISA notes it "might wait longer than strictly necessary" when the Matrix Unit is shared across threads. This trades a small amount of math-pipeline overlap for correctness, which is the same trade #52256 already made on the two generic Blackhole paths.

`STALLWAIT` holds until all selected conditions are simultaneously true, so a single combined mask is correct and sufficient; no extra instruction is added. This matters for the sites recorded into the replay buffer (`generalized_moe_gate_eltwise_binary`, the `deepseek_moe_gate` variants) where the recorded instruction count must not change — it does not.

## Affected sites

`p_stall::SRC?_VLD` → `p_stall::MATH | p_stall::SRC?_VLD`, preserving any existing `WAIT_SFPU`.

**Canonical LLK — Wormhole**
| File | Sites |
|---|---|
| `tt_llk_wormhole_b0/common/inc/cmath_common.h` | `move_d2a_row_broadcast_fixed_face`, `wait_bank_valid<SrcA>`, `wait_bank_valid<SrcB>` |
| `tt_llk_wormhole_b0/llk_lib/llk_math_transpose_dest.h` | `_llk_math_transpose_dest_` |
| `tt_llk_wormhole_b0/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_generalized_moe_gate_eltwise_binary.h` | RELOAD replay sequence |
| `tt_llk_wormhole_b0/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_generalized_moe_gate_transpose_dest_single_face.h` | `copy4rows`, `step1_hi`, `step0`, `step1`, `step2` |

**Canonical LLK — Blackhole**
| File | Sites |
|---|---|
| `tt_llk_blackhole/common/inc/cmath_common.h` | `move_d2a_row_broadcast_fixed_face`, `wait_bank_valid<SrcA>`, `wait_bank_valid<SrcB>` |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/llk_math_transpose_dest.h` | `_llk_math_transpose_dest_` |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_generalized_moe_gate_transpose_dest_single_face.h` | `copy4rows`, `step1_hi`, `step0`, `step1`, `step2` |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_face_compressed_mm.h` | split-partial merge |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_rmsnorm_bcast_scalar_dest_reuse.h` | `rmsnorm_bcast_scalar_reuse_dest_as_src` |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_sdpa_bcast_col_srcb_reuse.h` | preamble |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_sdpa_bcast_col_srca_srcb_reuse.h` | preamble |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_sdpa_custom_mm_reuse_dest_srcb.h` | main loop |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/experimental/llk_math_custom_mm_reuse_dest_srcb.h` | main loop |

**TTNN-private LLK copies** under `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/experimental/deepseek/moe/deepseek_moe_gate/device/kernel_includes/tt_llk/`
| File | Sites |
|---|---|
| `tt_llk_wormhole_b0/llk_lib/llk_math_deepseek_moe_gate_eltwise_binary.h` | `DEST_TO_SRCA`, `DEST_TO_SRCB` |
| `tt_llk_wormhole_b0/llk_lib/llk_math_deepseek_moe_gate_transpose_dest_single_face.h` | `step0`, `step1`, `step2` |
| `tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/llk_math_deepseek_moe_gate_transpose_dest_single_face.h` | `step0`, `step1`, `step2` |

These private copies are compiled by the TTNN DeepSeek MoE gate operation, so fixing only the canonical headers would leave the production path defective — the same trap called out in #53655. PR #53690 covers the Blackhole `deepseek_moe_gate_eltwise_binary` copy; the Wormhole copy and both `transpose_dest_single_face` copies are not covered by any PR.

Two of the sites (`move_d2a_row_broadcast_fixed_face`, `wait_bank_valid<>`) currently have no callers in the repository. They are included because they are pre-broken templates: the defect ships the moment something calls them.

## Out of scope

Excluded because another PR already owns them:

- `tt_llk_wormhole_b0/common/inc/cmath_common.h` `move_d2a_fixed_face` / `move_d2b_fixed_face` — open PR #54731
- `tt_llk_blackhole/.../llk_math_deepseek_moe_gate_eltwise_binary.h`, `tt_llk_blackhole/.../llk_math_generalized_moe_gate_eltwise_binary.h`, and the TTNN-private Blackhole `deepseek_moe_gate_eltwise_binary` copy — open PR #53690 (issue #53655)
- `tt_llk_blackhole/common/inc/cmath_common.h` `move_d2a_fixed_face` / `move_d2b_fixed_face` — already fixed by merged PR #52256

Excluded because they are a different hazard, not this one:

- `llk_math_compressed_custom_mm.h` — the wait gates a `SETRWC` and a matmul replay, not a Dest→Src move
- `llk_math_sdpa_custom_mm.h` — the wait gates `MOVB2D`, which *reads* SrcB rather than writing it
- `ckernel_sfpu_topk_xl.h` — `STALL_CFG` waits around SFPU configuration
- All of Quasar — `move_d2a_fixed_face` / `move_d2b_fixed_face` / `llk_math_transpose_dest.h` / `llk_math_reduce.h` / `llk_math_unary_broadcast.h` carry the same bare waits, but Quasar's `STALLWAIT` has a different operand encoding and its bank handshake has not been assessed here. This needs a Quasar owner and a separate issue.

## Verification

The wait is a mask constant, so the change is behaviour-preserving except for the added drain, and it cannot alter recorded replay lengths.

The defect class is latent by nature — it produces a wrong value only when a bank flip is in flight at the wait, which no current test forces — so this is an inspection-and-ISA-grounded fix in the same mould as #53655/#53690, not a fail-without/pass-with reproduction. Blackhole regression coverage is available on this box and will be run. **The Wormhole sites cannot be executed here and need a Wormhole board before merge.**

## Follow-up

The TTNN-private LLK copies mean a fix to a canonical header silently misses production callers. @jasondavies raised the same point on #53655. Consolidating those copies onto the canonical implementation would prevent the next instance of this and is worth a separate issue.

items.title: [Gemma4/Wormhole] Deterministic garbled long-prose output at specific encoded lengths >=100k on T3K (12B & 31B); BH clean at same lengths
items.body:
## Summary
Gemma4 long-prose generation on **Wormhole T3K** produces deterministic garbled/degenerate output at specific encoded prompt lengths ≥ ~100k tokens. **WH-local**: Blackhole (emulated-LB Galaxy, 8-point walk 100,462–130,816 including 106,500 / 108,000 / 109,857) is clean at the same lengths. Both 31B and 12B affected at different points.

## Point map (branch `arg/gemma4_coherence_fix` @ c5e8d23845f, T3K, Frankenstein quote task, greedy, x2 byte-equality per point)
| model | encoded | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 31B | 91,052 / 97,097 / 100,462 / 104,954 | clean, byte-equal |
| 31B | **100,793** | GARBLED (`'s la's` loop), deterministic |
| 31B | **109,857** | GARBLED (`I had't been...`), deterministic |
| 31B | **127,574** | GARBLED (`lapped` flavor) |
| 12B | 12,288 / 16,384 / ~106k | clean |
| 12B | ~120k | coherent but rep-divergent |
| 12B | **127,574** | fully degenerate token salad |

Note the **non-monotonicity** (100,462 clean → 100,793 corrupt → 104,954 clean → 109,857 corrupt): there is no single length threshold.

## Evidence
- **Path-independent**: metal demo and vLLM serving produce *byte-identical* garble at 109,857 → in the shared model forward (prefill), not serving state.
- **Chunk-invariant**: `GEMMA4_PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE` 8192→4096 at 109,857 → byte-identical output. Not per-Q-chunk config ("absolute-position family").
- **Deterministic** per exact input (byte-equal across reps and across metal/server).
- **Build-stable**: 100,793 produces the identical `'s la's` loop on the pre-coherence-fix build.
- **Cross-platform control**: BH clean at these lengths (shared ledger §10).
- Ruled out: block-table width boundaries (98,304 = 1536 blocks crossed clean), 64k page-table width, prefill chunk count, sliding-stride multiples (98,304 = 6x16,384 clean).

## Suspect class
WH-conditional seq-len-dependent kernel/program config in the prefill path (precedent: `PREFILL_SDPA_HARD_MAX = 32768` — "non-chunked SDPA silently wrong past 2^15"). Static audit of gemma4 attention configs found no WH-conditional constant in the 100–130k range yet; the defect may live below the model layer (SDPA/matmul program-config selection at large cache_len on WH).

## Repro
`env -u CI MESH_DEVICE=T3K HF_MODEL=google/gemma-4-31B-it pytest models/demos/gemma4/demo/text_demo_v2.py -k long-context-128k` with the standard 128k prompt json (encodes to 100,793) → item B of the quote answer is a deterministic `'s la's` loop.

items.title: [Bug] layer_norm/rms_norm_pre_all_gather 2D core grid path: same wide-row L1 over-allocation, plus a hang at H=1024 W=1024
items.body:
### Summary

`LayerNormPreAllGather2DProgramFactory` (the `use_2d_core_grid=True` path) carries the same
per-row `x^2` buffer over-allocation that #54697 reports for the default factory, and hits the
same L1 limit at a wide `fp32_dest_acc_en` row.

Separately, and blocking validation of that path, the 2D path **hangs** on an ordinary shape.
Both are described below; the hang is the more serious of the two and may warrant its own issue.

### 1. L1 over-allocation at wide rows

```python
import torch, ttnn
dev = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0)
cfg = ttnn.WormholeComputeKernelConfig(
    math_fidelity=ttnn.MathFidelity.HiFi2, math_approx_mode=False,
    fp32_dest_acc_en=True, packer_l1_acc=True)
x  = torch.randn((1, 1, 32, 4096), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
tt = ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT,
                     device=dev, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
ttnn.rms_norm_pre_all_gather(tt, compute_kernel_config=cfg, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16,
                             use_2d_core_grid=True)
```

Observed on wormhole:

```
Statically allocated dataflow buffers ... grow to 1725632 B
which is beyond max L1 size of 1499136 B
```

Cause is the same as #54697: `intermed0_tiles = Wt * double_buffer_constant` sizes `x^2` at a
full row, doubled, and since #52081 that buffer is fp32 when `fp32_dest_acc_en` is set. The 2D
factory additionally allocates `PRE2D_X2_MERGE` (`cores_y` tiles), which is why its total is
slightly higher than the 1D path's 1684672 B at the same shape.

The 2D compute kernel (`layernorm_pre_allgather_2d.cpp`) has the same fill-to-`Wt`-then-single-
`BulkWaitBulkPop`-reduce structure as the 1D one, so the same adaptive sizing applies: keep the
double buffer where the program fits L1, fall back to a single buffer only where it does not.

Confirmed that works — with adaptive sizing applied to this factory:

| shape (`use_2d_core_grid=True`) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| H=32 W=1024 | runs | runs, PCC 0.9993 |
| H=32 W=2048 | runs | runs, PCC 0.9987 |
| H=32 W=4096 | **fails to allocate** | **runs, PCC 0.9977** |

Note the budget should be L1 above the reserved base
(`l1_size_per_core - get_base_allocator_addr(HalMemType::L1)`), matching what
`validate_dataflow_buffer_region` compares against, and should stay a function of shape/dtypes/
device config only — sizing from `lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address` would make the program
depend on state the program-cache key does not cover.

### 2. Pre-existing hang on a tall ordinary shape

The same call at `H=1024, W=1024` — a width well inside L1, nothing to do with the allocation
above — deadlocks the device:

```
TIMEOUT: device timeout, potential hang detected, the device is unrecoverable
```

This is **not** caused by any buffer-sizing change: it reproduces on an unmodified tree. It is
why the L1 fix above has not been landed for this path — a basic shape deadlocks before the path
can be characterised.

Reproduce by taking the snippet in section 1 and using `(1, 1, 1024, 1024)` for the input shape.
`TT_METAL_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=45` makes it fail fast instead of hanging indefinitely; the
device needs a `tt-smi -r` afterwards.

### Context

`use_2d_core_grid` is opt-in and is not set by any traced model configuration currently in the
sweeps, which is likely why neither problem has been noticed. #54697 / #54698 cover the default
factory only.

items.title: test_model.py: cache_pcc is unreachable, so the KV cache PCC gate has never run
items.body:
## Summary

`cache_pcc` in `models/tt_transformers/tests/test_model.py` has never evaluated. The KV cache comparison it guards, and the two threshold dicts that feed it, are dead code.

## Detail

```python
cache_pcc = layers == 1 and not dummy_weights
```

The test is parametrized `"weights, layers"` over exactly two pairs:

- `("random", 1)` → `dummy_weights=True` → `not dummy_weights` is `False`
- `("instruct", None)` → `layers == 1` is `False`

No pair satisfies both terms, so `cache_pcc` is `False` in every cell and the `if cache_pcc:` block never runs. This has been true since the flag was introduced in #21306 — the parametrize was already these two pairs at that commit, so the block has never executed.

Consequences:

- `final_k_cache_pcc` and `final_v_cache_pcc` (8 model entries each, 16 total) have never been compared against anything.
- A latent bug inside the block went unnoticed for the same reason: `reference_model.cache_k` / `.cache_v` were not subscripted by layer, while `HfModelWrapper.cache_k` returns a per-layer list. Fixed in #53816 so the block is correct if it is ever enabled, but it remains unreachable.

## Why it is worth enabling

The Galaxy copy of this test runs the equivalent comparison with `cache_pcc = layers == 1` (no dummy-weights term) and passes with K/V PCC `0.99987` against a `0.9997` threshold. So the comparison is meaningful even with random weights — the dummy-weights guard appears to be over-caution rather than a real constraint.

## Proposed fix

Drop the dummy-weights term to match Galaxy:

```python
cache_pcc = layers == 1
```

## Blast radius

Small. In the tiered registry only one leg runs `-k quick`:

- `Llama 3.2-90B-Vision unit tests` / `wh_llmbox_perf` (tier 2) — would newly arm `final_k_cache_pcc["Llama-3.2-90B"] = 0.9995` and `final_v_cache_pcc["Llama-3.2-90B"] = 0.9996`

The Llama 3.1-8B and Mistral-7B entries run `-k full`, where `layers=None`, so they stay off. `tests/scripts/run_python_model_tests.sh` also runs 8B `-k quick`, but has no workflow caller today.

Those two 90B thresholds have never been evaluated, so the enabling PR should expect to calibrate them rather than assume they hold. With `layers == 1` only one decoder layer is built, so the vision models' cross-attention layers (which have no `layer_past`) are not reached.

## Context

Found while reviewing #53816, which corrected the decode-position bug in this test and edited the unreachable block. That PR fixes the layer-indexing bug and documents the unreachability, but deliberately does not arm the thresholds — that belongs here.

items.title: Investigate how tests should be separated between tt-metal and tt-inference-server
items.body: We should investigate and define how tests should be organized for models across tt-metal and tt-inference-server repos. Since tt-inference-server already requires evals, benchmarks and specification tests as part of model release, should that repo be the primary location for model tests that ensure quality, correctness and performance; in which case tt-metal should contain only PCC tests? Or should tests be organized differently?

items.title: concat: sharded s2s uses absolute dim 2/3 instead of rank-relative H/W, silent wrong data on rank ≠ 4
items.body:
Item 4 from master ticket

## Problem

`ConcatS2SMultiProgramFactory` decides height vs width concat with the **absolute** index `2 == dim`. Height is supposed to be `dim == rank - 2`.

`operation_attributes.dim` is already **normalized**. For a rank-3 tensor, width concat (`dim=-1`) is **dim 2**, which is also `rank - 1`. The factory treats that as height concat: each input shard is stacked **below** the previous one instead of **beside** it.

`select_program_factory` has the same literals (`3 == args.dim` for the 2-tensor width factories, `2 == args.dim || 3 == args.dim` for s2s multi). Rank-3 width concat never hits the RM/tiled width factories and is forced into the multi factory with the wrong layout. Rank-5 sharded width (`dim == 4`) misses those paths entirely.

This is silent wrong data (in-bounds). With larger shard heights the bad write offsets can also go **OOB in L1**.

The sibling `ConcatBlockShardedProgramFactory` and the sharded validator already use `rank - 1` / `rank - 2`. `build_unsqueeze_concat()` (would lift rank < 4 to 4D) is defined in `concat.cpp` but **not** used in the massaged concat chain.

## Example

Rank-3 ROW_MAJOR HEIGHT_SHARDED, one core, `ttnn.concat([a, b], dim=-1)`:

| | Shape / result |
|--|----------------|
| Inputs | `(1, 4, 16)` + `(1, 4, 16)`, shard `(4, 16)` |
| Output shard | `(4, 32)` |
| PyTorch | columns 0–15 from `a`, 16–31 from `b` |
| Current ttnn | `a` in rows 0–1, `b` in rows 2–3, columns 16–31 **zero** |

Same case at rank 4, shape `(1, 1, 4, 16)`, `dim=3`: **correct**.

Larger height (e.g. 64 sticks, two equal inputs): second input starts at half the output shard; last stick lands ~1.5× the shard size → OOB L1 write.

## Location

- `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/concat/device/concat_s2s_multi_program_factory.cpp` — `is_height_concat = 2 == operation_attributes.dim`
- `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/concat/device/concat_device_operation.cpp` — `select_program_factory` (`3 == args.dim`, `2 == args.dim \|\| 3 == args.dim`)

## Suggested fix

Mirror the block-sharded factory:

```cpp
const uint32_t rank = input_tensors[0].logical_shape().rank();
const bool is_height_concat = rank >= 2 && operation_attributes.dim == rank - 2;
```

In `select_program_factory`, replace the dim literals with `args.dim == rank - 1` (width) and `args.dim == rank - 2` (height).

## Test plan

Add cases in `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/data_movement/test_concat.py`:

- Rank-3 HEIGHT_SHARDED width concat (`dim=-1`), 2 and 3 tensors (3 tensors hits the multi factory; 2-tensor RM width uses the RM factory after dispatch is fixed).
- Rank-3 WIDTH_SHARDED height concat (`dim=-2`).
- Rank-2 HEIGHT_SHARDED width concat (used to miss dim 2/3 dispatch).
- Compare shape and values against `torch.concat`.

items.title: ttnn.grid_sample accepts FLOAT32 input and returns unrelated values; BFLOAT16 input is correct
items.body:
`ttnn.grid_sample` validates FLOAT32 input as supported and runs without error, but the
values it returns bear no relation to the reference. The same call with BFLOAT16 input
is correct. Output is finite and bit-stable across runs, so nothing signals the problem.

## Observed

Wormhole n150 and Blackhole p150b, `main` at `d4ee647ae3c`. Input `(1, 32, 16, 16)`
NCHW fed as NHWC, grid `(1, 8, 8, 2)`, bilinear, `padding_mode="zeros"`,
`align_corners=False`. Every case returns the same shape `(1, 8, 8, 32)`.

First six output values, same input in every row:

| | values |
|---|---|
| `torch.nn.functional.grid_sample` | `0.3661, -0.0175, -0.4147, -0.5385, 2.1881, -0.0384` |
| BFLOAT16 input, n150 | `0.3691, -0.0144, -0.4082, -0.5391, 2.2031, -0.0386` |
| BFLOAT16 input, p150b | `0.3691, -0.0144, -0.4082, -0.5391, 2.2031, -0.0386` |
| **FLOAT32 input, n150** | `0.1631, -0.0386, -0.0571, -0.1826, 0.6250, -0.0400` |
| **FLOAT32 input, p150b** | `-0.4551, -1.1484, -0.2598, -0.0898, 0.3223, -0.4609` |

BFLOAT16 tracks the reference to bf16 precision and is bit-identical on both
architectures. FLOAT32 does not track it on either, **and the two architectures
disagree with each other**. A deterministic arithmetic error would give the same wrong
answer on both; a misaligned read gives whatever the stride lands on, which differs per
architecture. That is the strongest evidence here for where to look.

It is the input element size specifically, not the grid: a FLOAT32 **grid** with
BFLOAT16 input is correct. So the three cases are

- input bf16, grid bf16: correct
- input bf16, grid fp32: correct
- input fp32, grid fp32: wrong

Within one architecture the output is deterministic: five runs in each of two separate
processes produced a bit-identical result (same SHA1). It is stable and repeatable, just
wrong, and wrong in an architecture-dependent way.

## Where

Validation accepts FLOAT32 at
[`grid_sample_device_operation.cpp:93-94`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/grid_sample/device/grid_sample_device_operation.cpp#L93-L94):

```cpp
TT_FATAL(
    input_tensor.dtype() == DataType::BFLOAT16 || input_tensor.dtype() == DataType::FLOAT32,
    "Input tensor must be BFLOAT16 or FLOAT32");
```

The pattern points at 2-byte element assumptions in the reader and stick arithmetic:
the op reads the right number of *elements* but the wrong number of *bytes* per
element, so a 4-byte input is sampled at half stride.

## Why it matters

`models/experimental/uniad/tt/ttnn_utils.py:192-202` guards the sibling op against
exactly this, and its comment records the belief this issue disproves:

> The fused op requires all three inputs in bf16 (decomposed grid_sample tolerates
> fp32; this op does not). Most callers already emit bf16, but some e2e paths feed
> fp32 sampling locations / weights - guard each input.

grid_sample only appears to tolerate fp32. Any caller that trusts that and passes a
FLOAT32 input gets silently wrong samples.

## Repro

```python
import torch, ttnn

dev = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0)
torch.manual_seed(0)
inp = torch.randn(1, 32, 16, 16, dtype=torch.float32)
grid = torch.rand(1, 8, 8, 2, dtype=torch.float32) * 2 - 1

ref = torch.nn.functional.grid_sample(
    inp, grid, mode="bilinear", padding_mode="zeros", align_corners=False)
print("torch  ", ref.permute(0, 2, 3, 1).reshape(-1)[:6].tolist())

for dt in (ttnn.bfloat16, ttnn.float32):
    i = inp.permute(0, 2, 3, 1).contiguous()
    g = grid
    if dt == ttnn.bfloat16:
        i, g = i.to(torch.bfloat16), g.to(torch.bfloat16)
    a = ttnn.from_torch(i, dtype=dt, layout=ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT, device=dev)
    b = ttnn.from_torch(g, dtype=dt, layout=ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT, device=dev)
    out = ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.grid_sample(a, b)).float()
    print(str(dt), out.reshape(-1)[:6].tolist())
```

## Expected

Either produce correct values for FLOAT32 input, or reject it in validation so the
failure is loud. The current combination, accepted and silently wrong, is the worst of
the three.

## Related, and distinct

- #51226 audits three defects in `pool/`, two of them in `pool/rotate` with the same
  element-size flavour. None is in `pool/grid_sample`.
- The op has not been modified since 2026-07-31, so this is not a recent regression.

---

I'd like to take this through the bounty program and implement the fix myself. Holding off on a PR pending assignment.

items.title: tt_dit weight cache silently drops non-Parameter module state
items.body:
## Summary

`models/tt_dit/layers/module.py` has an unstated invariant that does not hold:

> `Module.load(cache_dir)` should leave a module in the same state as `Module.load_torch_state_dict(checkpoint)`.

It holds only for `named_parameters()`. Any host-side value a module derives from the checkpoint inside `_prepare_torch_state` is invisible to the weight cache and is **not** recomputed on load — it silently reverts to whatever the constructor set. No error, no shape mismatch, no log line.

One instance of this destroyed prompt adherence in the LTX-2.5 text encoder on every cached run. It is fixed. Four independent ad-hoc workarounds for the same root cause now exist in the tree (§4), and the framework still permits the failure mode (§6).

---

## 1. Mechanism

- `Module.__setattr__` (`module.py:75`) registers `Module` and `Parameter` instances into `_children` / `_parameters` and **explicitly drops everything else** from those registries (the `else` branch at `:94-98`).
- `Module.save` (`module.py:213`) walks children and parameters and writes one `.tensorbin` each.
- `Module.load` (`module.py:223`) walks the same two registries — and **never calls `_prepare_torch_state`**.

The parameter round trip itself is fine. `Parameter.save`/`load` (`module.py:452`/`:455`) are `ttnn.dump_tensor(mode=LOCAL)` / `ttnn.load_tensor`, verified on a 4x8 mesh for replicated, 1-D-sharded (both axes) and 2-D-sharded parameters. `Parameter._check_data` validates placement, dtype, layout, memory config and shape (against `local_shape`, `:505`); `mesh_axes` is the one declared property it does not check.

Skipping `_prepare_torch_state` on the cache path is *correct* for almost everything it does — renaming keys, reshaping for TT layout, fusing QKV, synthesizing keys, discarding keys with no TT home. All of that is pure translation whose only durable output is `Parameter._data`, which the cache does persist. It is fatal only for the one thing that writes to `self`.

## 2. The site that caused visible damage

`models/tt_dit/encoders/gemma4/model_gemma.py`, `Gemma4EncoderLayer`:

```python
self.layer_scalar = 1.0                                    # :477  constructor default
...
scalar = state.pop("layer_scalar", None)                   # :486  torch path ONLY
if scalar is not None:
    self.layer_scalar = float(scalar.reshape(-1)[0].item())
...
if self.layer_scalar != 1.0:                               # :527  forward
    hidden_states = ttnn.multiply(hidden_states, self.layer_scalar)
```

The LTX-2.5 Gemma-4 checkpoint (`text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-bf16.safetensors`) carries **48 of these, one per encoder layer, and not one is 1.0**:

```
0.0530 0.1660 0.2559 0.5156 0.3770 0.3555 0.3457 0.2969 0.2012 0.1270 0.1040 0.0045
0.7461 0.6445 0.9258 0.6562 0.7656 0.8203 0.8203 0.7773 0.6328 0.7344 0.7891 0.7930
0.8594 0.8672 0.6953 0.7383 0.7188 0.6602 0.7578 0.7070 0.5469 0.6328 0.7656 0.7773
0.8320 0.8516 0.8320 0.8594 0.8086 0.7969 0.8945 0.8281 0.8398 0.7461 0.6016 0.0498

min 0.0045   max 0.9258   mean 0.6161   product 6.0e-16
```

On a cached run all 48 are 1.0, so the `!= 1.0` guard makes `forward` skip the multiply **entirely** for every layer. The text embedding is destroyed. **The resulting video decodes as perfectly valid 1080p H.264 — it just does not follow its prompt.**

## 3. Why it went unnoticed for so long

Five runs, identical source, identical prompts, identical `noise_seed`:

| run | weight cache | prompt adherence |
|---|---|---|
| A | 9 HIT / 0 MISS | WRONG |
| B | **0 HIT / 9 MISS** | **CORRECT** |
| C | 9 HIT / 0 MISS | WRONG |
| D | 8 HIT / 1 MISS (encoder converted, cache rewritten) | CORRECT |
| E | 9 HIT / 0 MISS (post-fix) | **CORRECT** |

The cache happened to be empty when B started, so B converted every model from safetensors — and B is the only pre-fix run whose video followed its prompt.

Gray-frame PCC put A and C at 92–99% against an existing baseline and B at 9–34% against everything, which read as *"A and C reproduce the known-good baseline, B is the outlier."* **That was exactly backwards.** The baseline had itself been produced by a cached run, so the agreement between A, C and the baseline only ever showed that the cached path is *consistently* wrong. It was caught by watching the videos.

> **A pixel/PCC comparison against a cached-run baseline is structurally incapable of detecting this class of bug** — every cached run agrees with every other cached run. The check has to be that the cache round trip reproduces the **torch** load.

This is the most transferable finding here, and the reason no existing test caught it.

## 4. Where the workarounds are, exactly

Four independent per-class hacks for one root cause. Nobody had connected them until now.

| # | location | mechanism | fails how, on a stale cache |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `models/tt_dit/encoders/gemma4/model_gemma.py:497` (`save`) / `:510` (`load`) | writes `{prefix}layer_scalar.json` beside the `.tensorbin` files | **hard `LoadingError`** — deliberate; the silent 1.0 default is the bug |
| 2 | `models/tt_dit/models/transformers/transformer_mochi.py:494` (`save`) / `:504` (`load`) | `torch.save`/`torch.load` of `{prefix}pos_frequencies.pt`, `time_embed.pt`, `rope.pt` | `FileNotFoundError` — loud, but incidental |
| 3 | `models/tt_dit/models/transformers/wan2_2/transformer_wan.py:379` (`save`) / `:387` (`load`) | `torch.save`/`torch.load` of `{prefix}rope.pt` | `FileNotFoundError` — loud, but incidental |
| 4 | `models/tt_dit/models/audio_vae/audio_decoder_ltx.py:279-284` | **caller-side**: re-opens the safetensors file after *every* `cache.load_model` and calls `MelDecoder.set_per_channel_stats` (`mel_decoder_ltx.py:378`) | silent — falls back to `torch.ones`/`torch.zeros` |

Notes:

- **#1** is committed. `Gemma4EncoderLayer.load` refuses rather than defaulting, so a warm pre-fix LTX-2.5 gemma4 cache must be deleted (`rm -rf "$TT_DIT_CACHE_DIR"/gemma4-*/text_encoder`, ~67 s to rebuild). CI is unaffected — the jobs with a persistent `TT_DIT_CACHE_DIR` are Wan2.2 and LTX-2.3, and LTX-2.3 uses the **gemma3** encoder (`pipelines/ltx/pipeline_ltx.py:26`); only `pipelines/ltx/pipeline_ltx25_distilled.py` uses gemma4.
- **#2 and #3** absorb by *mutation* (`self.rope.load_state_dict(pop_substate(state, "rope"))`), not by rebinding an attribute, so they do not show up in the scan in §6.
- **#4** is the oldest, and `set_per_channel_stats`'s own docstring names the weight cache as its reason to exist. Two soft spots: it lives in the **caller**, so any other path that constructs a `MelDecoder` silently gets the identity defaults (`mel_decoder_ltx.py:302-303`); and the two routes disagree on dtype — `set_per_channel_stats:385` does `.float()`, `_prepare_torch_state:370` does not.

## 5. Sites assessed and found *not* defective

Two further absorption sites were checked against the actual checkpoints. Neither is a live bug — recording the evidence so nobody re-opens them.

**`models/tt_dit/layers/audio_resample.py:103` and `:193` — `_taps_cpu`. Not a bug.**

Both absorb a checkpoint `filter` key, falling back to the constructor's analytically computed kaiser-sinc kernel (`:95`, `:172`/`:181`). The checkpoint does carry the key — 400 `.filter` tensors in `vae/ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors` — so they genuinely are absorbed and lost on a cached run. But **all 400 are the same 12-tap constant, and it is the analytic kernel rounded to bf16**:

```
ckpt   [0.00203, 0.0094,  -0.02551, -0.05762, 0.12891, 0.44336, ...]   (400 keys, 1 distinct value)
analyt [0.00203, 0.00939, -0.02554, -0.05766, 0.12857, 0.44321, ...]
max|diff| = 3.3e-4      sum ratio = 1.0011
```

The cached path falls back to the fp32 analytic kernel — marginally *more* accurate than the bf16 copy in the checkpoint. The two paths are not bit-identical, and neither is wrong. The BWE resampler (`models/audio_vae/bwe_ltx.py:233`, `UpSample1d(window="hann")`) has no matching key at all and never absorbs.

**`models/tt_dit/models/audio_vae/mel_decoder_ltx.py:370`, `:372` — `_stats_std` / `_stats_mean`.** Real absorption, but worked around by #4 above, so the shipped audio path is correct.

## 6. The exposure that remains

There are ~100 `_prepare_torch_state` overrides in `models/tt_dit`; any of them can absorb checkpoint state onto `self` and lose it on every cached run, silently. Nothing detects it.

The rule for reviewers:

> **An assignment to `self.<attr>` inside `_prepare_torch_state` or `load_torch_state_dict` will not survive the weight cache.** Make it a `Parameter`, or persist it explicitly with a `save`/`load` override that hard-errors when its sidecar is missing.

To re-run the inventory:

```python
import ast, pathlib
for p in sorted(pathlib.Path("models/tt_dit").rglob("*.py")):
    try: tree = ast.parse(p.read_text())
    except SyntaxError: continue
    for n in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in ("_prepare_torch_state", "load_torch_state_dict"):
            for a in ast.walk(n):
                if (isinstance(a, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(a.ctx, ast.Store)
                        and isinstance(getattr(a, "value", None), ast.Name) and a.value.id == "self"):
                    print(f"{p}:{a.lineno}  self.{a.attr}")
```

Current output — the four real sites plus two known false positives:

```
models/tt_dit/encoders/gemma4/model_gemma.py:488     self.layer_scalar
models/tt_dit/layers/audio_resample.py:103           self._taps_cpu
models/tt_dit/layers/audio_resample.py:193           self._taps_cpu
models/tt_dit/models/audio_vae/mel_decoder_ltx.py:370  self._stats_std
models/tt_dit/models/audio_vae/mel_decoder_ltx.py:372  self._stats_mean
models/tt_dit/models/vae/vae_qwenimage.py:61         self.wan_decoder     # plumbing, false positive
models/tt_dit/models/vae/vae_qwenimage.py:63         self._is_loaded      # plumbing, false positive
```

It does **not** catch absorption by mutation — workarounds #2 and #3 in §4.

## 7. The obvious detector does not work — don't rebuild it

The natural idea is to watch the state dict and infer what the module must have kept:

```python
before = {id(v) for v in state_dict.values()}
self._prepare_torch_state(state_dict)
absorbed = before - {id(v) for v in state_dict.values()}   # DOES NOT WORK
```

The premise is that a renamed tensor keeps its identity (true — `rename_substate` re-inserts the same object) while an absorbed one vanishes. But so does a **replaced** one: `state[k] = <anything new>` drops the old object from `.values()` and is indistinguishable from absorption. Of the 104 `_prepare_torch_state` / `load_torch_state_dict` definitions in `models/tt_dit`, **54 transform tensors** and **11 delete keys outright**. The counter-example that settles it is `layers/normalization.py:66`:

```python
state["weight"] = state["weight"].unsqueeze(0)
```

Every model in the tree has norm layers, so this detector fires on every model. Making it usable would mean annotating ~54 transform sites and 11 discard sites — a far larger migration than the bug it guards.

This also dissolves the "absorb vs. discard are indistinguishable" problem, which looked like the central design question: it only exists because the probe watches the checkpoint. A discard changes no module attribute; an absorption does.

## 8. Suggested solutions

Roughly in order of value per unit of work.

### 8a. Probe `self`, not the state dict

Diff the module's own plain attributes across the hook call. An attribute that changed while `_prepare_torch_state` ran is checkpoint-derived by construction, because the checkpoint is that function's only input.

```python
# module.py, _load_torch_state_dict_inner, replacing the bare call at :136
state_dict = dict(state_dict)
before = dict(self.__dict__)
self._prepare_torch_state(state_dict)
for name, value in self.__dict__.items():
    if name in _INTERNAL or isinstance(value, (Module, Parameter)):
        continue
    if name not in before or before[name] is not value:
        ...   # raise, or auto-register for save/load
```

Properties: needs **no edits to any of the ~100 existing hooks**, has no false positives from tensor transforms, and needs no absorb-vs-discard spelling. Authors write nothing new — `self.layer_scalar = float(...)` is already the right code and simply starts being noticed.

Two variants:

- **Raise.** Hard error at conversion time naming the module and attribute, with the four known sites carrying explicit opt-outs. A new module that absorbs checkpoint state fails on its first conversion, in its own unit test, with no cache involved. Smallest possible change: no new file format, no manifest, cache layout untouched.
- **Auto-persist.** Register the changed attributes into a third registry alongside `_children`/`_parameters`, and have `save`/`load` carry them. Removes the need for per-class sidecars entirely, at the cost of a serialization format and a serializability guard.

Known gap either way: it detects **rebinding**, not **mutation**, so workarounds #2/#3 in §4 stay invisible to it and would need an explicit declaration.

### 8b. Migrate to `Parameter` where the shape and consumer allow

`Parameter` is already registered, saved and loaded, and a missing `.tensorbin` already produces a `LoadingError` — i.e. the stale-cache hard error comes for free, with no manifest and no sidecar.

Fits `layer_scalar` well (it would drop the `!= 1.0` guard and make the multiply a tensor broadcast; the text encoder runs once per prompt, so the cost is nil). Does **not** fit everything:

- `mel_decoder`'s stats have a **checkpoint-dependent length** (`C` or `C*F`, see `_denormalize_latents:403-407`) and `Parameter` requires a fixed `total_shape` at construction.
- `_taps_cpu` and the mel stats are consumed by **host** code — `depthwise_tap_filter` (`audio_ops.py:185-194`) does `len(taps)`, uses `tuple(taps)` as a dict cache key and calls `torch.tensor(taps, ...)`; `_denormalize_latents` is plain host torch. A device Parameter needs a memoized readback.
- `Parameter` has **no default**, and both audio sites are optional keys with meaningful fallbacks. Workable by synthesizing the computed default into the state dict inside `_prepare_torch_state` — precedent at `transformer_mochi.py:518` (`state["fracture_spatial_input.weight"] = torch.eye(...)`) — which also lets the mel stats be normalized to one fixed shape at load time instead of branching on the decode path.
- mochi/wan hold whole torch `nn.Module`s; not expressible as one `Parameter` without flattening each tensor.

### 8c. One generic equivalence test

There is no test anywhere that compares the two load paths against each other. That absence is the root reason a bug that inverted the text encoder went unnoticed. `models/tt_dit/tests/unit/test_module.py::test_save_and_load` is the closest, but `TinyFeedForward` holds only `Parameter`s, so it can only ever exercise the part of the round trip that already works.

## 9. How this would be tested

### 9a. Generic: the cache round trip must reproduce the torch load

The assertion that actually characterises the bug. Parameterize over the cached models rather than writing one test per class.

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("mesh_device", [(1, 1)], ids=["1x1"], indirect=["mesh_device"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("build", [build_gemma4_layer, build_mel_decoder, ...])
def test_cache_round_trip_matches_torch_load(mesh_device, build):
    state = synthetic_state_dict_for(build)      # or a real slice of the checkpoint

    converted = build(mesh_device)
    converted.load_torch_state_dict(state)       # path A: torch

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        converted.save(d)
        cached = build(mesh_device)
        cached.load(d)                           # path B: cache

    # parameters
    for (name, p_a), (_, p_b) in zip(converted.named_parameters(), cached.named_parameters()):
        assert ttnn.to_torch(p_a.data).equal(ttnn.to_torch(p_b.data)), name

    # everything else: the part the cache silently drops today
    assert host_attrs(converted) == host_attrs(cached)

def host_attrs(module):
    """Plain (non-Module, non-Parameter) attributes, recursively, keyed by dotted path."""
    out = {}
    for name, value in module.__dict__.items():
        if name.startswith("_") and name in INTERNAL: continue
        if isinstance(value, (Module, Parameter)): continue
        if is_comparable(value):  out[name] = value
    for name, child in module.named_children():
        out.update({f"{name}.{k}": v for k, v in host_attrs(child).items()})
    return out
```

One test file catches all four current sites and every future one. The important property is that it never compares a cached run to another cached run.

### 9b. A stale cache must be refused, not silently defaulted

```python
def test_cache_missing_host_state_is_refused(mesh_device, expect_error):
    layer = build_gemma4_layer(mesh_device)
    layer._prepare_torch_state({"layer_scalar": torch.tensor([0.0045])})

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        layer.save(d, prefix="layers.0.")
        (Path(d) / "layers.0.layer_scalar.json").unlink()      # or .tensorbin, under 8b
        with expect_error(LoadingError, "layer_scalar"):
            build_gemma4_layer(mesh_device).load(d, prefix="layers.0.")
```

Use the `expect_error` fixture (`conftest.py:910`), not `pytest.raises` — the repo's `prefer-expect-error` pre-commit hook rejects the latter.

### 9c. The detector itself (if 8a lands)

Device-free, and the one that makes the bug unwritable:

```python
def test_absorbing_checkpoint_state_is_rejected():
    class Absorber(Module):
        def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.scale = 1.0
        def _prepare_torch_state(self, state): self.scale = float(state.pop("scale"))
        def forward(self): ...

    with pytest.raises(HostStateError, match="Absorber.*scale"):
        Absorber().load_torch_state_dict({"scale": torch.tensor([0.5])})

def test_transforming_the_state_dict_is_not_flagged():
    """The false positive that kills the state-dict probe (normalization.py:66)."""
    class Reshaper(Module):
        def __init__(self, d): super().__init__(); self.weight = Parameter(total_shape=[1, d], device=d)
        def _prepare_torch_state(self, state): state["weight"] = state["weight"].unsqueeze(0)
        def forward(self): ...

    Reshaper(...).load_torch_state_dict({"weight": torch.randn(8)})   # must not raise
```

Choosing a value like `0.0045` (the smallest of the 48 real scalars) rather than something near the default matters — a test value close to `1.0` would pass even with the bug present.

Unit level, once a round-trip test exists (needs one device):

```bash
pytest models/tt_dit/tests/unit/test_module.py
```

End to end (~12 min per run, needs a 4x8 Blackhole):

```bash
export LTX25_ROOT=<LTX-2.5 snapshot dir>
export DIFFVAE_CHECKPOINT=$LTX25_ROOT/vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors
LTX_VAE_TIME=1 LTX_TRACED=1 OUTPUT_PATH=$PWD/generated/check.mp4 \

DIFFVAE_TP_HEADS=1 DIFFVAE_SLAB_FRAMES=73 \

```

To see the original bug: revert the `save`/`load` override, `rm -rf "$TT_DIT_CACHE_DIR"/gemma4-*/text_encoder`, run once (correct video), run again (cached — wrong video). With the fix in place that same deletion instead exercises the refusal path.

items.title: Make KDA work for multi-turn scenario
items.body:
### Context
Multi-turn prefill resumes at the KV offset the last turn ended on. K3 is only correct when that offset is a multiple of the 5120-token chunk. At any other offset the chunk runs to completion, its own output is close to right, and the `KdaState` it hands the next chunk is uncorrelated with the truth: `KdaState.recurrent` PCC 0.0156 at offset 640 and -0.0085 at offset 2592, against 0.9999 when chunk-aligned. No exception, assert, hang or NaN — pure accuracy issue.

## Layout and terms

A chunk is 5120 tokens over the 8 SP chips, `chunk_local = 640` each. Token position `p` sits on chip `(p // 640) % 8`. `rotated_chip_positions` (`tt/mla/utils.py`) reports which position each chip's rows carry; both tables come from it.

**Chip order**: the order chips must be composed in to follow the token sequence. Both `KdaState` combinators iterate `range(sp_size)`, which is correct only if chip 0 holds the chunk's first tokens.

**Split chip**: a chip holding two token ranges that are not adjacent in the sequence. It is the chip the chunk starts on, carrying both the chunk's head and its tail. `offset % 640` decides whether one exists:

* `== 0`: chunk starts on a block boundary, covers 8 blocks of 640, one per chip. No split.
* `!= 0`: chunk starts mid-block, covers 9 partial blocks over 8 chips, so head and tail land on the same chip. Exactly one split.

Starting chip and split chip are different things. Every chunk has a starting chip; only a mid-block chunk also has a split.

Offset 0:

```
covers [0, 5120)
  chip 0: [0, 640)   chip 1: [640, 1280)  ...  chip 7: [4480, 5120)
  chip order [0..7], no split
```

Offset 2592 (`% 640 = 32`, mid-block):

```
covers [2592, 7712)
  chip 4: [2592, 3200) and [7680, 7712)      two ranges, 4480 apart
  chip 5: [3200, 3840)  ...  chip 3: [7040, 7680)
  chip order [4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3], chip 4 split
```

Offset 13440 (`% 640 = 0`, block-aligned but not chunk-aligned):

```
covers [13440, 18560)
  chip 5: [13440, 14080)  chip 6: [14080, 14720)  ...  chip 4: [17920, 18560)
  chip order [5,6,7,0,1,2,3,4], no split
```

Chips are rotated here, so composition must start at chip 5, but each still holds one range.

## Repro

`_PADDED_MID_15K` is the per-chunk real-token list `[2592, 1568, 5120, 800, 3360, 1920]` that CI runs for K2.6 in `test_kimi_prefill_transformer_chunked_padded`. Its running sums are the resume offsets. On K3:

| chunk | offset | `% 640` | chip order | split chip | K3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | from chip 0 | none | correct |
| 1 | 2592 | 32 | from chip 4 | chip 4 | `KdaState` uncorrelated |
| 2 | 4160 | 320 | from chip 6 | chip 6 | `KdaState` uncorrelated |
| 3 | 9280 | 320 | from chip 6 | chip 6 | `KdaState` uncorrelated |
| 4 | 10080 | 480 | from chip 7 | chip 7 | `KdaState` uncorrelated |
| 5 | 13440 | 0 | from chip 5 | none | `KdaState` uncorrelated |

One chunk of six is correct, so the K2.6/GLM padded-accuracy test cannot be run against K3.

"Uncorrelated" is PCC near zero against the same tokens in sequence order, measured rather than inferred. See the acceptance test below.

## Acceptance test

A runnable statement of what "supported" means. Not on `main`: it lives on branch `feature/kimi-k3-prefill` (PR #54850), at [`models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tests/kda/model/test_multiturn_resume.py`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/8d02110c29222090ad6c9c17d9bb54f4bf0506f0/models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tests/kda/model/test_multiturn_resume.py).

```
git fetch origin feature/kimi-k3-prefill && git checkout feature/kimi-k3-prefill
pytest models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tests/kda/model/test_multiturn_resume.py -k fabric2d -v
```

Needs an 8x4 Blackhole Galaxy. The file is self-contained: synthetic weights and a torch reference, no checkpoint or golden trace.

Same 5120 tokens at every offset; only the chip layout changes, taken from `rotated_chip_positions`. The reference is those tokens in sequence order, from the same zero `KdaState` with the same weights, so any PCC drop is ordering alone. Measured on 8x4 fabric2d today:

| resume offset | `% 640` | starts on | output PCC | `KdaState.recurrent` | `KdaState.convolution` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | chip 0 | 0.999947 | 0.999882 | 0.999997 |
| 640 | 0 | chip 1 | 0.999370 | **0.015634** | **0.011901** |
| 2592 | 32 | chip 4 | 0.998508 | **-0.008461** | **-0.006189** |

Both halves of `KdaState` are checked. `KdaState.convolution` comes from `convolution_halo` and `KdaState.recurrent` from `_distributed_affine_prefix`, and both are uncorrelated at both broken offsets, so this is not specific to one combinator.

Output and `KdaState` disagree, and that is the useful part. The offending chunk's own output stays near 0.999, because decay makes each position depend mostly on its neighbours. `KdaState`, which is the entire point of a chunk under multi-turn, is uncorrelated. The damage is not in the chunk that resumes, it is in the one after it, which is why a per-chunk output check does not find this.

The two non-zero offsets are `xfail(strict=True)`. A fix makes them XPASS and the markers come off.

## Padding

A turn ends mid-chunk, so its last chunk is a 5120-wide tile with only the first N tokens real.

`ttKDA.forward` has no valid-length argument. Nothing in `tt/kda/` or `reference/kda/` does.

KDA therefore integrates the pad rows as if they were tokens, and both halves of `KdaState` carry them into the next turn.

PCC of `KdaState` after a padded tile, against the same real tokens with no padding:

| real tokens of 5120 | `KdaState.recurrent` | `KdaState.convolution` |
|---|---|---|
| 2592 | -0.0366 | 0.0149 |
| 5088 | 0.0025 | 0.0693 |

32 pad tokens are enough, and 32 is the floor because turn lengths are tile-aligned. Decay is `exp(gate)` per step with `gate` in (-5, 0), so 32 steps scale the real prefix by up to `exp(-160)`, leaving a state built from the pad rows.

## Ordering

Both combinators assume chip order is sequence order:

* `convolution_halo` (`tt/kda/ops.py:104-130`): chip `r`'s entry state comes from chip `r-1`'s tail; the outgoing state comes from chip `sp-1`.
* `_distributed_affine_prefix` (`tt/kda/ops.py:727-728`): composes per-chip affine summaries over `range(sp_size)`.

Two things go wrong, and they are independent. Wrong composition order applies to every non-chunk-aligned offset. A split chip is an extra problem on top, only when `% 640 != 0`.

| offset | chip order | split | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| n * 5120 | from chip 0 | none | correct: composition order matches device order |
| n * 640 | from chip `(offset/640) % 8` | none | wrong order alone, measured 0.0156 at offset 640 |
| tile-aligned only | starts mid-block | one | wrong order, and one chip that no reordering fixes |

So `% 640 == 0` avoids the split but not the failure: the chunk still starts on a chip other than 0, and both combinators still compose 0..7.

A split chip is not just an ordering problem. `_distributed_affine_prefix` reduces each chip to one affine `(A, B)` advancing `KdaState` across its tokens, which holds for one contiguous range. The split chip has two, separated by 4480 tokens of other chips' work, so no single `(A, B)` describes it and reordering cannot fix it.

Current workaround: round each resume down to a whole chunk and replay the remainder, up to 5119 tokens per turn.

items.title: Blackhole L1 counter names point at the wrong clients, and five count nothing at all
items.body:
## What happens

Around thirty Blackhole L1 client names in `hw_counters.h` do not describe the interface they actually count, and five of them count nothing at all. Anyone reading an L1 counter column on Blackhole can be looking at a different client than the name suggests.

## The two problems

**Names that point at the wrong client.** Attributing grants per interface across the isolate run types (an interface busy only in `UNPACK_ISOLATE` belongs to unpack, only in `PACK_ISOLATE` to pack) disagrees with several declared names. Examples:

| declared | what the traffic says |
|---|---|
| `L1_1_RISC_CORE` | pack driven, not RISC |
| `L1_2_NOC_RING2_PORT_0..3` | unpack driven |
| `L1_3_NOC_RING3_PORT_4..6` | pack driven |
| `L1_0_UNIFIED_PACKER` | matches the unpacker port 1 counter on the Wormhole side |

The ring numbering is also wrong in principle. Blackhole has two NOCs, so names implying rings 2 and 3 cannot be describing what they claim.

**Five entries count nothing.** Confirmed against the Blackhole RTL. The L1 counter mux selects a group of eight interfaces, group four covers interfaces 32 to 39, and interfaces 35 and above are tied to zero in the two NOC configuration that Blackhole uses. That makes the last five entries of group four dead, and they currently carry names as though they were real.

Earlier captures showed non zero grants on those five, but that was the mux defect that made every group read group zero's data, not real traffic.

## Scope

- Correct the Blackhole L1 client names in `hw_counters.h`.
- Remove the five dead entries from the group four array.
- Update the two consumer sites in `tools/tracy/perf_counter_analysis.py` that refer to the old names.
- Note in the docs that these identities are measured rather than taken from a specification.

## Not in scope

Wormhole. Its sixteen interfaces are all real, there are no tied off ports, and its two groups map cleanly, so nothing needs renaming there.

## Care needed

One metric column keeps its name while changing which interface it measures. That has to be called out in the PR, since a consumer tracking it over time would see a step change with no name change to explain it. Consider renaming the column instead.
